correctness.rationale: Unique factorization gives the six-variable Euler product. The degree-1 terms of logarithms cancel, the unique deficit-one bidegree-2 correction is exactly -q \(e2(x)e2(y)\), and all m>=3 log terms have q-degree <=m-2. The full exp remainder has deficit at least two. Coefficient extraction then gives \(M_d\) and -9\(N_d\). Elementary inclusion-exclusion gives \(M_d\)=(d+1)(d+2)(d²+3d+4)/8 and \(N_d\)=d(d+1)(d+2)(3d+1)/24. Exact-recurrence-style enumeration independently tests the two matrix counts and small finite fields. Scope fixed d, q arbitrary prime power, and finite checks are not proof.

value.rationale: The October 2026 four-factor formula motivates the first higher (six-factor) restricted multiplicative energy, with separate equal-degree constraints. Its explicit first correction is a nontrivial arithmetic quantity controlled by 3x3 shifted transportation margins; the main Birkhoff lattice-point term alone is known and would not suffice. The result enables quantitative first-order correction for every fixed d, without claiming uniformity in d or a higher-factor theorem.
